theorem_statement: The ordinary random walk and Hashimoto walk are related by an exact conditioning law. After the first edge, ordinary walking has K=12 choices and nonbacktracking walking has K-1=11 choices, so the survival ratio for n-edge paths is ((K-1)/K)^(n-1), and the entropy defect is log(12/11). The same branch K-1=11 is recovered as tr(A_L^2)/(2E), as Wiener/QLE, and as the Hashimoto Perron eigenvalue. Ihara-Bass places the restricted Hashimoto roots on |x|=sqrt(11).
interpretive_note: This closes the ordinary-to-nonbacktracking gap. The Markov channel gives probabilities, the line graph counts two-step turns, Hashimoto orients and conditions them, and Matrix Tree records the global connectivity entropy.
